We value your privacy

We use cookies to enhance your browsing experience, serve personalized ads or content, and analyze our traffic. By clicking "Accept All", you consent to our use of cookies.

Customize Reject All Accept All

Customize Consent Preferences![Image 10](https://cdn-cookieyes.com/assets/images/close.svg)

We use cookies to help you navigate efficiently and perform certain functions. You will find detailed information about all cookies under each consent category below.

The cookies that are categorized as "Necessary" are stored on your browser as they are essential for enabling the basic functionalities of the site. ...Show more

Necessary Always Active

Necessary cookies are required to enable the basic features of this site, such as providing secure log-in or adjusting your consent preferences. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable data.

*   Cookie m 
*   Duration 2 years 
*   Description Stripe sets this cookie for fraud prevention purposes. It identifies the device used to access the website, allowing the website to be formatted accordingly. 

*   Cookie __stripe_mid 
*   Duration 1 year 
*   Description Stripe sets this cookie to process payments. 

*   Cookie __stripe_sid 
*   Duration 1 hour 
*   Description Stripe sets this cookie to process payments. 

*   Cookie __cf_bm 
*   Duration 1 hour 
*   Description This cookie, set by Cloudflare, is used to support Cloudflare Bot Management.  

*   Cookie rc::a 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description This cookie is set by the Google recaptcha service to identify bots to protect the website against malicious spam attacks. 

*   Cookie rc::c 
*   Duration session 
*   Description This cookie is set by the Google recaptcha service to identify bots to protect the website against malicious spam attacks. 

*   Cookie dd_cookie_test_* 
*   Duration 1 minute 
*   Description Datadog Real User Monitoring (RUM) Browser SDK sets this cookie as a temporary cookie used to test for cookie support.  

*   Cookie cookieyes-consent 
*   Duration 1 year 
*   Description CookieYes sets this cookie to remember users' consent preferences so that their preferences are respected on subsequent visits to this site. It does not collect or store any personal information about the site visitors. 

Functional

- [x] 

Functional cookies help perform certain functionalities like sharing the content of the website on social media platforms, collecting feedback, and other third-party features.

*   Cookie __cmpcc 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 
*   Description The Consent Manager sets this cookie for website options and services. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-device-id 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description YouTube sets this cookie to store the user's video preferences using embedded YouTube videos. 

*   Cookie ytidb::LAST_RESULT_ENTRY_KEY 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description The cookie ytidb::LAST_RESULT_ENTRY_KEY is used by YouTube to store the last search result entry that was clicked by the user. This information is used to improve the user experience by providing more relevant search results in the future. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-connected-devices 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description YouTube sets this cookie to store the user's video preferences using embedded YouTube videos. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-session-app 
*   Duration session 
*   Description The yt-remote-session-app cookie is used by YouTube to store user preferences and information about the interface of the embedded YouTube video player. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-cast-installed 
*   Duration session 
*   Description The yt-remote-cast-installed cookie is used to store the user's video player preferences using embedded YouTube video. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-session-name 
*   Duration session 
*   Description The yt-remote-session-name cookie is used by YouTube to store the user's video player preferences using embedded YouTube video. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-cast-available 
*   Duration session 
*   Description The yt-remote-cast-available cookie is used to store the user's preferences regarding whether casting is available on their YouTube video player. 

*   Cookie yt-remote-fast-check-period 
*   Duration session 
*   Description The yt-remote-fast-check-period cookie is used by YouTube to store the user's video player preferences for embedded YouTube videos. 

*   Cookie mid 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description The mid cookie is set by Instagram to personalise user experience by remembering user preferences and settings. 

Analytics

- [x] 

Analytical cookies are used to understand how visitors interact with the website. These cookies help provide information on metrics such as the number of visitors, bounce rate, traffic source, etc.

*   Cookie _ga 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description Google Analytics sets this cookie to calculate visitor, session and campaign data and track site usage for the site's analytics report. The cookie stores information anonymously and assigns a randomly generated number to recognise unique visitors. 

*   Cookie _gid 
*   Duration 1 day 
*   Description Google Analytics sets this cookie to store information on how visitors use a website while also creating an analytics report of the website's performance. Some of the collected data includes the number of visitors, their source, and the pages they visit anonymously. 

*   Cookie _ga_* 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description Google Analytics sets this cookie to store and count page views. 

*   Cookie _fbp 
*   Duration 3 months 
*   Description Facebook sets this cookie to display advertisements when either on Facebook or on a digital platform powered by Facebook advertising after visiting the website. 

*   Cookie uid 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description This is a Google UserID cookie that tracks users across various website segments. 

*   Cookie sid 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description The sid cookie contains digitally signed and encrypted records of a user’s Google account ID and most recent sign-in time. 

*   Cookie vuid 
*   Duration 1 year 1 month 4 days 
*   Description Vimeo installs this cookie to collect tracking information by setting a unique ID to embed videos on the website.  

*   Cookie CLID 
*   Duration 1 year 
*   Description Microsoft Clarity set this cookie to store information about how visitors interact with the website. The cookie helps to provide an analysis report. The data collection includes the number of visitors, where they visit the website, and the pages visited. 

*   Cookie ajs_anonymous_id 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description This cookie is set by Segment to count the number of people who visit a certain site by tracking if they have visited before. 

Performance

- [x] 

Performance cookies are used to understand and analyze the key performance indexes of the website which helps in delivering a better user experience for the visitors.

*   Cookie _gat 
*   Duration 1 minute 
*   Description Google Universal Analytics sets this cookie to restrain request rate and thus limit data collection on high-traffic sites. 

*   Cookie loglevel 
*   Duration Never Expires 
*   Description Squarespace sets this cookie to maintain settings and outputs when using the Developer Tools Console on the current session. 

Advertisement

- [x] 

Advertisement cookies are used to provide visitors with customized advertisements based on the pages you visited previously and to analyze the effectiveness of the ad campaigns.

*   Cookie YSC 
*   Duration session 
*   Description Youtube sets this cookie to track the views of embedded videos on Youtube pages. 

*   Cookie VISITOR_INFO1_LIVE 
*   Duration 6 months 
*   Description YouTube sets this cookie to measure bandwidth, determining whether the user gets the new or old player interface. 

*   Cookie VISITOR_PRIVACY_METADATA 
*   Duration 6 months 
*   Description YouTube sets this cookie to store the user's cookie consent state for the current domain.  

Uncategorized

- [x] 

Other uncategorized cookies are those that are being analyzed and have not been classified into a category as yet.

*   Cookie loopyloyalty_referrer 
*   Duration 6 months 
*   Description Description is currently not available. 

*   Cookie recent_write 
*   Duration Less than a minute 
*   Description Description is currently not available. 

*   Cookie gtm_id 
*   Duration 1 year 
*   Description No description available. 

*   Cookie _cfuvid 
*   Duration session 
*   Description Description is currently not available. 

*   Cookie TAPSESSID 
*   Duration 14 days 
*   Description Description is currently not available.

results.title: How Much Does a Loyalty Program Cost? (2026)
results.markdown:
Title: How Much Does a Loyalty Program Cost? (2026)

URL Source: https://authors.loop.fans/blog/how-much-does-a-loyalty-program-cost

Published Time: 2026-06-29T17:41:49.157191+00:00

Markdown Content:
The cost of a loyalty program depends on how it works and what your business needs to operate it. A simple digital card may have very different costs from a multi-location program with messaging, POS integrations, paid rewards, and dedicated support. Compare the full cost of the program, not just the advertised subscription.

## Include every cost category

*   **Software:** subscription, member or location limits, and plan upgrades.
*   **Setup:** onboarding, design, configuration, data migration, and training.
*   **Rewards:** product cost, discounts, fulfillment, breakage, and any partner-funded offers.
*   **Communication:** SMS fees, email volume, push tools, and campaign creation.
*   **Integrations and equipment:** POS connections, tablets, scanners, or payment hardware.
*   **Operations:** staff time, customer support, reporting, and program management.
*   **Exit costs:** data export, contract termination, customer re-enrollment, or switching systems.

## Set the scope before asking for quotes

Tell each provider how many locations you have, the approximate member volume, the behaviors you want to reward, the systems you already use, and whether you need referrals, UGC, communications, or coalition partners. Ask for an itemized quote and identify what requires an upgraded tier or an additional fee.

## Budget rewards separately from software

Estimate the cost of each reward based on expected redemptions, not just points issued. Include the margin impact of discounts and the fulfillment cost of products or experiences. If a partner contributes a reward, confirm the agreement, availability, and responsibilities in writing.

## Compare cost with a measurable goal

Choose an outcome such as repeat visits, customer retention, referrals, or increased participation. Estimate the program’s contribution using your own customer and transaction data, and include the full operating cost in the calculation. Avoid assuming every member purchase was caused by loyalty.

## Use a simple monthly model

**Total monthly cost** = software + reward cost + communications + integrations/equipment + staff time + other fees. Compare that with a clearly defined value measure, such as incremental gross margin from repeat behavior. Track assumptions separately so you can revise them when real results arrive.

Loop Fans publishes its current per-venue and network options on the [pricing page](https://loop.fans/pricing). For program design, see our [small-business loyalty guide](https://authors.loop.fans/blog/loyalty-programs-for-small-businesses) and [loyalty program ROI guide](https://authors.loop.fans/blog/loyalty-program-roi).

## Compare the right kind of program

A paper punch card, a digital card for one venue and a district-wide coalition are different purchases. A single café may need check-ins, a reachable milestone and a way to see repeat visits. A restaurant may need loyalty linked to its reservation and guest follow-up. A BID or DMO needs merchant onboarding, shared program rules, reporting across locations and a clear funding model. Ask vendors to quote the same scope before comparing their monthly prices.

Write down the number of locations, active members, expected messages, staff users, reward types, integrations and reporting needs. Then identify which are included, which cost extra and which require staff work. A low software fee can be expensive if setup and manual administration are high; a larger subscription can be reasonable if it replaces several tools you already pay for.

## Fixed costs, variable costs and one-time costs

| Cost | What to ask | How to estimate it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Software subscription | What member, venue and message limits apply? Is the price monthly or annual? | Use the tier that fits expected use, not only the launch month. |
| Setup and migration | Who imports contacts, creates rewards and trains staff? | Include vendor fees and staff hours. |
| Reward fulfilment | Who pays for the item, discount, experience or access? | Forecast redemptions times the true marginal cost of each reward. |
| Messaging | Are email or SMS sends included? Is consent managed? | Estimate sends per active member, then price overages. |
| Integration | Does the program need a POS, booking system, website or CRM connection? | Separate one-time implementation from ongoing maintenance. |
| Operations | Who checks fraud, answers member questions and updates offers? | Budget staff time every month. |
| Promotion | How will customers discover and join? | Include signage, staff prompts, email and launch activity. |

For a multi-business program, add partner recruitment, training and a process for settling shared rewards. If a visitor earns at one venue and spends at another, the partners need agreed rules on who funds the redemption, how it is recorded and how disputes are handled. The [coalition launch guide](https://loop.fans/blog/launch-coalition-loyalty-program) covers that operating work.

## A worked example for a single venue

Suppose a café estimates 300 active members. It plans to offer a free drink after a set number of eligible visits. To make a budget, the owner should estimate the monthly software fee, the incremental cost of drinks likely to be redeemed, staff time for explaining and processing the program, and any messaging cost. The retail price of a drink is not the same as its marginal fulfilment cost; use the amount the business actually spends to deliver it.

Assume, purely for illustration, that the owner expects 30 redemptions a month at a $2 marginal cost each, two hours of staff administration at $25 an hour, and $40 of software and messaging. The estimated monthly cost is $150: $60 for rewards, $50 for staff time and $40 for tools. If the café expects 20 additional visits, it should compare the incremental gross margin from those visits with $150. A $10 sale is not $10 of profit. If each additional visit contributes $6 of gross margin, 20 visits contribute $120, leaving the program below break-even on that narrow measure. If it also improves repeat frequency or referrals, those outcomes should be counted only when observed.

This example is a model, not a typical café result or a Loop price quote. Change the assumptions to match your own location and monitor actual redemptions. The [loyalty ROI calculator](https://loop.fans/free-tools/loyalty-roi-calculator) can help you work through the inputs.

## A different budget for a BID or destination

A district program has two customers: the public who participate and the businesses that need value from joining. The software may include a digital passport, coalition rewards or reporting, but the operating budget must also cover merchant onboarding, campaign content, signs or QR codes, reward funding and a person who resolves day-to-day issues. Decide whether the district, individual merchants or sponsors fund each reward.

A DMO may want to measure visitor dispersal, member discovery and itinerary activity, while a BID may care about cross-visits and levy-payer value. Those are not identical to a venue's repeat-purchase metric. Report people who joined, businesses viewed, check-ins, reward claims, verified redemptions and confirmed bookings where an integration supplies confirmation. Do not count a booking link click as revenue. See the [connected region guide](https://loop.fans/blog/connected-region-visitor-journey-guide) and [BID loyalty guide](https://loop.fans/blog/bid-loyalty-program) for the design decisions.

Loop lists the [full destination platform from $5,000 per year](https://loop.fans/pricing). Its standalone AI Trip Planner has separate pricing and is included in the full destination platform. Make sure a quote states exactly which products, locations, member limits and setup services it covers.

## Questions to ask before signing

1.   **What happens when we grow?** Ask what changes at the next member, venue or message threshold.
2.   **What does “active member” mean?** Vendors may define it differently. Request the exact billing definition.
3.   **Can we export our data?** Ask for the format, frequency and cost of export.
4.   **Can customers join without another app?** Test the join and redemption flow on a phone.
5.   **How are rewards verified?** A reward should be simple to claim and difficult to abuse.
6.   **Which transactions can be confirmed?** Identify what comes from your POS or booking provider and what is only a click.
7.   **Who owns implementation?** Ask whether copy, artwork, onboarding and staff training are included.
8.   **How can we leave?** Read cancellation terms and understand what happens to outstanding rewards.

## Judge the program by margin and participation

Start with a clear goal: more second visits, higher returning r
